jobs.title: Head of Marketing
jobs.description:
We believe general-purpose, generally-intelligent robots will be built in our lifetimes. Robots will work in our factories, move our goods, walk on our streets and eventually be in our homes. To build that future, research and deployment must work in lockstep: real-world operation must make the technology better and better technology must make deployment easier. We're looking for the thinkers, builders, and researchers who want to be part of that loop.
As an AI robotics frontier lab that deploys its inventions directly into the facilities that need them, on state-of-the-art hardware, every line of code or piece of copy written at Tutor has a direct impact on the global, physical economy.

Culture
We believe that something truly special can happen when talented, motivated people work together; at Tutor, every member of our team is empowered to have real impact in everything that they do. We’re characterized by both technical excellence and a focus on collaboration and respect.

The Role
We're hiring Tutor's first Head of Marketing : the leader who will define our category, own our narrative, and build the marketing engine and organization for an AI robotics company with robots working in production today.

Tutor is in a rare position. We're an AI robotics lab with a deployed, revenue-generating fleet and a loyal customer base — very early to a category most companies are still demoing. We have two distinct motions to power: a high-velocity mid-market business selling to manufacturers and co-packers, and a growing enterprise business built on seven-figure programs with major logistics and consumer brands. Marketing today is early and largely embedded in Sales; your mandate is to turn it into a strategic function that compounds — process-, technology-, and numbers-driven rather than powered by individual heroics.

You'll report directly to the CEO, sit on the leadership team, and own the full stack: category and brand, product marketing, demand generation, events, and PR/communications. You'll inherit and grow a small team into a large organization building and executing a new playbook for general proliferation of AI robotics.

This is a player-coach role. We're looking for a builder who still makes things, not an operator who needs a large org and agency bench to function. And we're an AI company: we expect you to build an AI-native marketing organization where an elite team produces at unusual scale.
Responsibilities
Strategy & Ownership of the Number

- Define Tutor's marketing strategy across both motions and own marketing's contribution to revenue: pipeline sourced and influenced, measured honestly.

- Establish the measurement and attribution discipline to know what's working — across trade shows, campaigns, content, and PR — and reallocate accordingly.

- Operate as a full member of the leadership team in tight partnership with the Head of Sales on a shared pipeline.

Category & Brand

- Own Tutor's narrative and positioning: cement our position in public and industry awareness and lay claim to the category while our timing advantage lasts.

- Build a quarterly event/PR drumbeat, anchored by a flagship annual Tutor event serving press, enterprise relationship-building, and pipeline.

- Systematize founder-led thought leadership and decide how our research and product milestones get told to press, analysts, and the community.

- Bring coherence to our brand and product architecture as the product line expands.

Product Marketing

- Oversee messaging, customer proof, and sales enablement across product lines and buyer types

- Ensure every deployment turns into marketing assets: case studies by default, quantified ROI stories, and vertical collateral in daily use by the sales team.

Demand Generation

- Build the vertical demand engine for the mid-market motion: vertical landing pages, content, nurture, and inbound that make our core products progressively lower-friction to sell.

- Stand up account-based marketing for the enterprise motion with Sales: target-account strategy, executive-level content and programs, and air cover for our largest pursuits.

Team & AI-Native Operations

- Recruit and lead a small, exceptional team amplified by AI agents — collateral production, research, and campaign operations largely run on pipelines the team designs.

- Own the marketing budget and vendor/agency relationships, with a bias toward building capability in-house.
Qualifications
- 10+ years in B2B marketing with experience scaling a marketing function 1→N at a startup (0→1 experience a strong plus) — you've built the machine, not just run one.

- Experience bringing a novel product category to market , creating demand rather than competing for existing search volume in a crowded space.

- Full-stack marketer with a strong product marketing core and real depth in demand generation, events, and PR/brand/category communications.

- Experience across both mid-market velocity and high-touch, high-value enterprise motions.

- Experience marketing to non-technical operational buyers (plant, operations, and supply chain leadership).

- A track record of tight, trusted partnership with sales leadership on a shared pipeline number.

- AI-native : software-capable or deeply curious, already using AI as leverage in your work, and excited to build a marketing org around it.

- High-agency, creative, and spiky — strong opinions, distinctive work, and a bias to ship.

- Based in / willing to relocate to the Boston area — this role is in person at our Watertown HQ; travel up to ~20% (customer sites, trade shows), though likely less.

You're probably not a fit if your playbook is primarily paid-channel demand gen, if you're a brand leader who doesn't own pipeline, or if you've only operated inside large marketing organizations with big teams and agency support.
Preferred Experience
- Supply chain (manufacturing, logistics), industrial automation, or robotics — warehouse automation or supply chain services likely the best fit.

- Marketing capital equipment, hardware, or other considered physical-product purchases.

- Building or scaling flagship owned events and executive/community programs.

jobs.title: Supply Chain Manager — Sonny V2
jobs.description:
About Tutor

We believe general-purpose, generally-intelligent robots will be built in our lifetimes. Robots will work in our factories, move our goods, walk on our streets and eventually be in our homes. To build that future, research and deployment must work in lockstep: real-world operation must make the technology better, and better technology must make deployment easier.

As an AI robotics company that deploys its inventions directly into the facilities that need them, on state-of-the-art hardware, every part we buy and every robot we ship has a direct impact on the global, physical economy. Founded by MIT alumni and backed by leading AI and robotics investors, we don't just build robots — we deploy, maintain, and continuously improve them in production environments.

Culture

We believe something truly special happens when talented, motivated people work together. At Tutor, every member of the team is empowered to have real impact in everything they do. We're characterized by both technical excellence and next-level collaboration and respect.
The Role
We're scaling to 1,000+ robots by 2028, and Sonny ramps in Q2 2027. You'll own its purchased-part supply chain end to end: the vendor base, the buys, the buffers, the cost, and the data that tells the company what we can build and when. Our critical parts come from China with 100+ day lead times, and the design is still changing monthly.  We are only as good as our suppliers  — you're the person who makes that work.

We want someone as comfortable in a spreadsheet as on a call with a factory in Shenzhen. Someone who builds the tools that predict shortages instead of chasing them, and who negotiates like every dollar and every day matters — because at our scale it does. Mindset and ownership over credentials.
What You'll Own
- The Sonny V2 vendor base.  Source, qualify, and manage suppliers for every purchased part on the Sonny V2 BOM. Lead second-sourcing on single-point-of-failure parts. Build real partnerships with critical suppliers, not just transactional relationships.

- The buy.  Own purchase orders, buffer strategy, and material coverage against the build plan. Decide when to bulk-order for lead-time insurance, when to air freight, and when to hold. Attach controlled drawings and revs to every PO on a critical part — no exceptions.

- Clear to Build.  Build and maintain the predictive tools the company relies on: clear-to-build reports (now / 30 / 60 / 90 days), shortage callouts, lead-time trackers, and material risk dashboards pulled from ION and the build forecast. Supply Chain should get actionable buy signals from these tools, and so should Engineering and Sales.

- Cost and negotiation.  Drive unit cost, payment terms, MOQs, and lead times down through structured negotiation. Own landed cost and COGS visibility for the product.

- Design change absorption.  BOM and design changes on Sonny will keep coming on a cadence greater than zero. Work directly with Production Engineering and R&D through the ECO process so the supply chain absorbs changes at monthly build cutovers rather than stalling the line.

- Outsourcing strategy.  Evaluate and stand up outsourced sub-assembly and contract-manufacturing options as Sonny volume grows, including offshore options.

- Supplier performance.  Track on-time delivery, quality (NCMRs back to the vendor), and responsiveness. Escalate early and hard when a supplier slips.

- The system of record.  Keep ION accurate: part numbers, unit costs, purchased assemblies, on-order quantities, and inventory so the shop floor and the finance team see the same truth.
What We're Looking For
- 5+ years in supply chain, purchasing, or strategic sourcing for a hardware product, ideally through a new-product-introduction ramp (prototype → pilot → production)

- Hands-on experience sourcing from and managing Chinese vendors: factory qualification, PI/T/T payment structures, EXW and freight tradeoffs (sea vs. air), customs, and the reality of time-zone and communication gaps

- A proven negotiator with examples of cost, lead-time, MOQ, or terms wins you personally drove

- Strong analytical and tool-building skills: you've built clear-to-build, MRP-style, or shortage-forecasting tools in Excel, SQL, Python, or a BI tool — not just consumed them

- Fluency with an MES/ERP/PLM system (ION, NetSuite, Arena, Odoo, SAP, or similar) and comfort working from a controlled BOM with revision control

- Mechanical and electrical literacy: you can read a drawing, understand a harness spec, and talk to an engineer about why a tolerance matters to a supplier

- Willingness to be on the shop floor, in the warehouse, and occasionally on a plane to a supplier

- Bachelor's degree in supply chain, engineering, business, or equivalent experience

Nice to Have

- Mandarin or Cantonese fluency  — a real advantage in day-to-day work with our China-based suppliers

- Experience with robotics, automation, EV, drones, or other electromechanical products with motors, batteries, PCBAs, and sheet metal

- Prior experience setting up or managing a China-based sourcing presence or sourcing agent

- APICS / CPSM / CSCP certification or Lean Six Sigma training

- Experience with First Resonance ION specifically

- Contract manufacturing / EMS outsourcing experience
How We Work — Our Values in This Role
We hire against our values, and we'll interview you against them too. Here's what they look like in this seat:

- Love of the Game.  You think building the supply chain for a brand-new robot is a genuinely cool problem, and you want to work with people who think so too.

- Gumption.  You don't wait for a PO request to show up. You see the build plan, spot the gap, and go close it.

- Beginner's Mindset.  You ask why a part costs what it costs and why the lead time is what it is. You experiment with new suppliers and new terms, and you're fine being wrong sometimes if it makes us better.

- Belief in Each Other.  You hold suppliers and colleagues to a high bar and you're transparent when something is off — including with the engineer whose design change just broke your lead time.

- Keep Moving Forward.  With incomplete information and a changing BOM, you find the 80/20 path, make the smart bet, and keep the line fed.

- Customer Obsession.  A late part is a late robot, and a late robot is a customer who is not getting the ROI we promised. You never lose sight of what's at stake downstream.
